knowledge_point.title: Determining the Value of a Constant for Which a Given Linear System Is Consistent or Inconsistent

question.:question/problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=1 \\ 2x+(k+4)y &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & k+4 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & k+4 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & k & 1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=1 \\ ky &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=0,$ then the second equation is $0=1,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=0.$

question.:question/problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y &=4 \\ 3x+(k+3)y &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & 4 \\ 3 & k+3 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & 4 \\ 3 & k+3 & 6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & k & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y &=4 \\ ky &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=0,$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$, and we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $2x+2y=4.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=0.$
